texts.preamble: Gaddam Tirupathi Rao vs The State Of Telangana on 27 September, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.22111 Of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of habeas corpus declaring the action of respondent No.3 in detaining the detenu viz.,, Gaddam Ravindra Babu S/o Srinivas, now detained in Central Prison, Cherlapalli, Medchal - Malkajgiri District, as illegal by setting aside impugned order dated 15.07.2023 and for consequential direction to respondent No.3 to release the detenu. 3. Respondent No.3 passed the detention order dated 15.07.2023 against the detenu under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser KL,J & SKS,J Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Amendment Act No.13 of 2018) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986') under the category of 'Spurious Seed Offender' as defined under Section - 2 (l) of the Act No.1 of 1986. 4. The impugned detention order was passed by respondent No.3 - detaining authority relying on the following two (02) crimes: Crime No. Offences Allegations leveled Remarks 285/22 of Section - 420 r/w 34 The detenu and his associates Conditional Choutuppal PS IPC, Sec. 3 (1) of were caught while in bail was Seeds Control possession of 22 quintals of granted. Seeds Act, 1966 & processed the same at Charge sheet Sec.15(1) of Siddivinayaka Polish Mill in was filed. Environmental Damarcherla, Nalgonda (CC 877/23) Protection Act, 1986 District, in order to sell the said spurious seeds to innocent farmers of Telangana, Maharashtra State and made the farmers to believe that the cotton seeds sold by them yield good crop and, thus, cheated them. KL,J & SKS,J 5. 8. It is also mentioned in the detention order that the detenu has been indulging in clandestine business of selling spurious cotton seeds/banned HT cotton seeds to the innocent farmer community and thereby cheated them for his pecuniary benefits in the limits of Rachakonda Commissionerate and other parts of Telangana State and bordering States. Even though the detenu was arrested and remanded to judicial custody, he could not mend his attitude and has shown scant respect for the law by indulging in similar activities and has been selling spurious/banned cotton seeds to the farmer community habitually and repeatedly in Telangana and bordering States. 9. During the current year i.e., 2023, the detenu was involved in the aforesaid two (02) crimes i.e., Crime No.285 of 2023 and Crime No.104 of 2023. In the first crime, the detenu was arrested by the Police of Choutuppal Police Station and remanded him to judicial custody on 02.06.2023. However, he has obtained bail on imposing certain conditions and he was released on bail on 08.06.2023. KL,J & SKS,J Violating such conditions imposed by the Court concerned, again the detenu resorted to indulge in similar activities of spurious seed circulation and again he was arrested in the second crime by the Police of Narketpally Police Station. Thus, the detenu was involved in couple of cases in quick succession within a period of week days from his release on bail in the first case. 10. The detaining authority also mentioned in the detention order that the HT Cotton was not approved by the Generic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) for commercial cultivation in India. Therefore, the sale, cultivation and seed production of HT cotton seed is illegal and punishable under Seeds Act, 1986, Seeds Rule, 1968, Seeds (Control) Order 1983. On account of illegal acts committed by the detenu in sale of spurious cotton seeds, the farmers, who purchased the same from the detenu and his associates for farming, incurred huge losses. They could not even earn back their investments. In the past earlier to the aforesaid two crimes, there were chances of frustrated farmers resorting to extreme measures, like suicides leaving their family members in a pathetic condition to lead their lives. There was also a possibility of enraged farmers attacking bogus seed companies and officials of agriculture department. The KL,J & SKS,J said incidents are criminal in nature and create panic among the public, especially the farmers' community and, thus, the activities of the detenu are prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' and also causing lot of panic in the minds of poor and small farmers' which will also have impact on the livelihood and their financial well- being. Apart from that, the acts of the detenu would certainly disturb the peace, tranquility and social harmony in the society, especially the farmers' community. In the light of the same, the detaining authority having considered the entire material on record arrived at the Gaddam Tirupathi Rao vs The State Of Telangana on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28752109/ 3 subjective satisfaction that the detenu is a 'spurious seed offender as defined in Section 2 (l) of the Act No.1 of 1986. Thus, with a view to prevent the detenu from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' respondent No.3 - detaining authority passed the impugned detention order dated 15.07.2023 and the same was approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.1046 of General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, dated 25.07.2023.
texts.arguments: Mr. Rapolu Bhaskar, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind. The detaining authority did not consider the material properly. Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order with regard to the alleged disturbance caused to the public order due to the alleged acts of the detenu. Thus, the detention order and the consequential approval order are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious and dangerous in nature and he has been habitually engaged in unlawful acts, such as clandestine business of procuring and selling of spurious cotton seeds/banned HT cotton seeds to the innocent farmers and make promising that the cotton seeds sold by them yields good crop. Thus, the detenu repeatedly cheats the poor and innocent farmers, who are put to irreparable losses and misery as the spurious seeds supplied by the detenu leads to very low and meager yield. The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only, passed the detention order KL,J & SKS,J in order to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences and the same was approved by respondent No.1. There is no error in it. i) He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2. 7. Perusal of detention order, dated 15.07.2023, passed by respondent No.3 would reveal that the detenu and his associates formed as gang and were procuring loose cotton seeds from farmers in Gaddam Tirupathi Rao vs The State Of Telangana on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28752109/ 2 Karnataka State at cheaper rate in huge quantity, transporting the same to 'Siddi Vinayaka Polish Mill' in Damarcharla of Nalgonda District, where they mixed with Imidacloprid, which made them into red in colour (Gaucho), packing them into small pouches and circulating in open market through their dealers with colourful labels. They are circulating spurious/banned HT cotton seeds in bulk quantity to Nagpur of Maharashtra state and other parts of Telangana State. Further, the detenu and his associates made to believe the local dealers, farmer community as it is BG-3 Type cotton seeds and yield good crop and, thus, he has been selling spurious/banned HT cotton . (1988) (1988) 1 SCC 296 KL,J & SKS,J seeds to farmers knowing fully-well that it does not yield any proper crop for his wrongful gain and thereby causing wrongful loss to gullible farmers. 11. Section - 2 (l) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "Spurious Seed Offender", which means any person who KL,J & SKS,J manufactures, stocks, sells or distributes any adulterated seeds or adulterate the original seeds by mixing low quality seeds or change the packing with the name of well known brands or does anything in contravention of any of the provisions of the Seeds Act, 1966 and the rules, notifications and orders made there-under or punishable under section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 who knowingly by himself or through any other person abets in any other manner the doing of any such things/offences; 12. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & SKS,J 14. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are. It will thus appear that just as "public Gaddam Tirupathi Rao vs The State Of Telangana on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28752109/ 4 order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". One has to imagine three concentric circles. It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'. At the same time, duty cast Gaddam Tirupathi Rao vs The State Of Telangana on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28752109/ 5 upon the 'State' as defined under Article - 12 of the Constitution of India to maintain law and order as well as public order.
